title: CDIF Access
description:
Profile module for machine-actionable access and usage conditions, expressed as ODRL Offer policies (odrlProperties/odrlOffer). Marks the catalog record as conformant to the CDIF access spec and requires at least one policy, attached in either of two places:
- on a schema:distribution item, as odrl:hasPolicy: the preferred place,
  because distributions of one dataset can carry different conditions
  (cdifbook data_access, "Connecting CDIF and ODRL"). The Offer may be
  inline or an {@id} reference.

- on the Dataset, as an {@id} reference in schema:conditionsOfAccess to
  a policy published elsewhere. Only a reference: cdifCore types the
  items of that property as string, {@id} or a CreativeWork link, and an
  inline Offer matches none of them, so it would fail any composite that
  includes cdifCore.

This module adds constraints only; it does not change cdifCore's schema:distribution anyOf [DataDownload, WebAPI]. Draft; OPEN QUESTIONS are marked "OPEN:".

dcterms:conformsTo.description: OPEN: https://w3id.org/cdif/access/1.1 is not minted. 1.1 follows the other CDIF modules; a new profile might start at 1.0 instead.

schema:conditionsOfAccess.description: Item shape comes from cdifCore. In a CDIF Access record, an {@id} item here should be the uid of an ODRL Offer; JSON Schema cannot tell that reference from any other (a SHACL rule would have to).

odrl:hasPolicy.description: ODRL policies governing access to and use of this distribution. OPEN: the book argues against dataset-level policies, so odrl:hasPolicy is not declared on the Dataset; confirm.

anyOf.title: ODRL Offer
anyOf.description:
An ODRL 2.2 Offer (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#policy-offer): the baseline access and usage conditions a data provider sets for a digital object, without naming who they apply to (that is an ODRL Agreement). Draft from the CDIF Access spreadsheet (CDIF_Access_Profile_ODRL_Classes_Properties_Description.xlsx) and the cdifbook data_access chapter.
Keys are ODRL's own compact terms (permission, target, action, ...), not prefixed CDIF keys, so a policy node carries its own @context, normally ["http://www.w3.org/ns/odrl.jsonld", {"cdifa1": "https://w3id.org/cdif/access/profile1/"}]. That context has no @vocab, so a cdifa1: action expands only if the policy's context declares the cdifa1 prefix.
An access condition (something done BEFORE the digital object is retrieved) is a permission duty constrained by event lt policyUsage (https://www.w3.org/TR/odrl-model/#duty-perm). Everything else is a usage condition: a permission (may do), an obligation (must do) or a prohibition (must not do).
OPEN QUESTIONS are marked "OPEN:" below.

@context.description: The ODRL context plus the cdifa1 prefix. Not constrained here: the same policy is valid with the context inherited from an enclosing document that already declares the ODRL terms.

@type.description: Always Offer, a subclass of odrl:Policy.

uid.description: Globally unique, resolvable IRI for this Offer; the ODRL context aliases uid to @id. A resolver should be able to return application/ld+json, not only an HTML page.

profile.description: The CDIF Access ODRL profile this policy uses, which supplies the cdifa1: actions the ODRL core vocabulary lacks (download, assent, datadestruction, ...). OPEN: nothing is published at this IRI yet, and it names a .ttl file where ODRL expects a profile identifier. The compact form is accepted because compaction under the cdifa1 prefix rewrites the full IRI to it.

assigner.description: The party issuing the Offer, normally the repository or data custodian. ODRL requires an assigner on an Offer; the spreadsheet does not list one yet. An IRI, or a party node identified by uid.

@type.description: Party, or PartyCollection for a group of users.

permission.description: Actions a user may perform on the target (usage conditions).

constraint.description: Who may exercise the permission, e.g. only users located in the UK. OPEN: the book's examples scope users with an assignee PartyCollection plus refinement instead; the spreadsheet uses constraints. Assignee is allowed (open world) but not modelled.

duty.description: Access conditions: actions that must be completed before the permitted action, e.g. assent to an End User Licence before download.

items.description: A permission duty carrying the accessConditionMarker. The spreadsheet gives the duty action as 1..*; ODRL allows one action per rule, so several pre-conditions are several duties. OPEN: the spreadsheet does not say what an assent duty assents to (e.g. which licence document); a duty target is one candidate.

contains.description: The constraint "event lt policyUsage": the duty must be fulfilled before the permission is exercised. In CDIF Access this is what marks a duty as an access condition. Each operand accepts the ODRL term, the odrl: compact IRI and the full IRI, because which one a document carries depends on how it was last compacted.

obligation.description: Actions every user of the target must perform, e.g. destroy the data at the end of a project. The spreadsheet gives 1..*; drafted as 0..* because an Offer with only permissions is common. OPEN: confirm.

prohibition.description: Actions a user must not perform, e.g. share TRE credentials.

ObjectReference.title: Object Reference
ObjectReference.description: A reference to a node defined elsewhere, by its @id.

Target.description: IRI of the asset the rule applies to: per the book, a distribution or data service rather than the dataset, since distributions of one dataset can carry different conditions. OPEN: ODRL AssetCollection for a policy covering several assets is not modelled yet.

Action.description: Either a term or compact IRI naming the action (cdifa1:download), or, when the action itself is narrowed, an object holding the action in rdf:value plus its refinements. OPEN: the cdifa1 action vocabulary is not defined, so values are not enumerated; whether it is an ODRL profile or a standalone controlled vocabulary is still to be settled.

Constraint.description: leftOperand operator rightOperand, e.g. spatial eq <country>. OPEN: the spreadsheet lists @type with cardinality 1 but gives no value and omits it on the access-condition constraint, so it is optional here; ODRL LogicalConstraint (and/or/xone) is not modelled. OPEN: no leftOperand, operator or rightOperand values are specified, so only the shape is checked.

rightOperand.description: A literal, a value object or an {@id} reference.
